nilpotent_QGF_removes_composite_layer.summary: Removes the composite-line layer and theta along Delta, P, M, R; along Q, S, K the same graphs return as s_X Psi bivalent vertices.
nilpotent_QGF_removes_composite_layer.mechanism_in_old_projects: Projects 1, 3, 4: non-minimal pair (cbar, b), gauge fermion Psi = -+ int cbar(d.A + xi b/2), antifield shift dPsi/dPhi, b eliminated (S_0 gets +1/2 (cbar^dd - d.A)^2/xi). Q^GF maps antifield slots to field slots only, so (Q^GF)^2 = 0, Im Q^GF = field Lagrangian, [Q,Q^GF] = -d^2 on every slot at xi = 1.
nilpotent_QGF_removes_composite_layer.argument: Composite kernel = 2 P* X P*, P* = Q^GF G, G = int_eps^T e^{-tH}. Along Delta it equals v.(P*)^2 + (P*)^2 v. (prop:c9-composite (i)), and (P*)^2 = (Q^GF)^2 G^2 = 0, so the A_V-c composite line and theta vanish (Psi is Poincare/scale/R invariant with weight(cbar) = 2). In general P* X P* = Q^GF G X Q^GF G vanishes iff X preserves the gauge-fixing Lagrangian; Q, S, K do not. Their terms appear as s_X Psi: (s_alpha V) d cbar (lambda-cbar line), 4 k.V cbar (V-cbar line), arity-two -1/2 cbar T cbar (alpha alphabar). The last is a negative control in project 3 check_master.log; it was missing at first and added later in project 2. No old project has a SUSY- or K-invariant gauge fixing; none exists off shell for N=4. Costello first-order YM [C07] also gives (Q^GF)^2 = 0, but no old project used it untwisted, and it has the same X-non-invariance.
nilpotent_QGF_removes_composite_layer.cost: New letters cbar, cbar^dd; c-cbar propagator replaces c-A^*; all Step-1 data (I^CT, log class Y, 27/16, Ob_3, F_3) to redo.
nilpotent_QGF_removes_composite_layer.gain: Costello axioms (3),(5) hold, so [C07 Lemma 6.5.1, 6.6.2] apply directly; theta disappears along Delta, P, M, R. No gain for Q_1, S_1, K_1.

recommendations.text: The non-minimal gauge (projects 1, 3, 4) is the only nilpotent untwisted Q^GF on this machine; it kills theta along Delta, P, M, R but moves the Q, S, K composite lines into s_X Psi vertices. Cheap test without switching: split each composite kernel P* X P* into a (Q^GF)^2 part and an 'X moves the slice' part; only the first should be theta-like.

(i) Profile-variation test (project 2 report6): replace e^{-eps p^2} by chi(eps p^2) and keep c_E[chi] and the rational moments as independent symbols; claimed scheme-independent combinations (27/4 - 8L; t_xi+ + t_xi- - t_P = 27/4 + 2L) must be chi-independent. (ii) Add second-order composite counterterms (c Phi)^fin_CT to the freedom table before calling a combination invariant (project 3: -1/12 + (3/2)L was removable only that way).

Adopt the project 3 check design: machine Q table = (S_0,.); Q^2, (Q^GF)^2, [Q,Q^GF] = H on all coordinates; Schwinger-Dyson inverse; master equation with negative controls; displayed formulas re-evaluated against data. Unit tests: (-1)^{|O|} O D = D O; Delta_eps(Phi Phi^dd) = -(-1)^{|Phi|} K_eps(x,x); odd-derivation insertion order; identical-leg averaging; no id()-keyed caches; residual checks after sympy.solve.

Build the classical part of Phi from antifield-completed twisted letters (project 2 ftilde, psitilde; project 6 b, beta, dictionary, homotopy h); compare at class level, d_1 on H(s_tw), so that scheme freedom and logs drop out. First target: the Konishi class, coefficient sqrt2 g^2 C C lambdabar lambdabar in units hbar/16pi^2 (projects 2 and 6, BK).

Compare the current two-body 4L(B_2+B_3) with project 1's xi = 1 scalar-pair kernels (G_fullBV/out/q_pair_kernels.json) after a dictionary, once it is confirmed that project G's Pi_O has no finite composite counterterm on the probe pair.
